items.description: R-9: raul TUI tab-bar overflow render path diverges from tab_hit_test. At narrow widths (< 60 cols with all 7 lanes), render_tab_bar (crates/raul/src/tui/render.rs:194-260) emits only a subset of tabs around the active lane plus arrow indicators and ellipses, but tab_hit_test (crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:207) assumes a contiguous left-to-right layout of ALL lanes starting at column 1. A mouse click on a partially-hidden tab lands on the wrong lane or misses. Keyboard nav is unaffected. Same class as R-3 (render vs hit-test divergence) but structural, not just compact-mode. Correct fix: extract the visible-window layout computed inside render_tab_bar into a shared helper that both render and handle_mouse/tab_hit_test call, so hit-testing knows which tabs were actually drawn and at which columns. Low real-world blast radius (narrow terminal + 7 lanes + mouse only).

items.description: Sort bug (M100+ regression, missed sites): the prior numeric-sort fix (commit db63821) only patched commands/list.rs:109 (mp list milestones) and sync.rs. Several sibling sort sites still order milestone ids with lexicographic .cmp() on the string, so ids >= 100 sort between 10 and 11. REPRODUCED on master: 'mp list steps --format json' emits milestones in order 100,101,102,103,95,96,97 (string sort: '1' < '9') instead of 95,96,97,100,101,102,103. Root cause: store::list_milestone_paths (store.rs:351) and list_archived_milestones (store.rs:678) sort filenames with paths.sort() (lexicographic); any consumer that does not re-sort numerically inherits the bug. CONFIRMED BUGGY SITES (all sort milestone ids as strings): (1) crates/mp/src/commands/list.rs:203 — mp list steps, sorts milestone id via ma.cmp(mb) then step id; should use paths::compare_milestone_ids for the milestone component. (2) crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:112 — pending_reviews sort by milestone_id string. (3) crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:148 and :149 — execution_pending and spec_review sorts by milestone_id string (affects mp reviews status / suggested_next pick). (4) crates/mp/src/plan_diff.rs:170 — HandhandBaseline milestone_index sort by id string. (5) crates/mp/src/plan_diff.rs:176 — snaps sort by id string. (6) crates/mp/src/plan_diff.rs:345 — milestone diff out sort by id string. (7) crates/mp/src/plan_diff.rs:406 — milestones_added_since sort by id string. (8) crates/mp/src/plan_diff.rs:447 — diff_milestone_files_since sort by id string (affects mp plan diff / handoff baseline). VERIFIED NOT BUGGY: specs.rs:34 (sorts domain.id, not milestone id), path_prefs.rs:79 (defers to baseline order via position(), not string cmp), challenge.rs:151 (challenge ids F-XX), step.rs:323 / path_engine.rs:72 (use compare_step_ids correctly), store.rs scenario/session sorts (not milestone ids). Fix pattern is mechanical: each a.id.cmp(&b.id) / a.milestone_id.cmp(&b.milestone_id) on a milestone id should become paths::compare_milestone_ids(&a.id, &b.id). Also consider fixing the root: list_milestone_paths / list_archived_milestones could sort by milestone_sort_key(filename) so downstream callers don't need to remember to re-sort. Add a regression test that builds a fixture with ids 99, 100, 101 and asserts every list/diff/reviews output is numerically ordered.

items.description: F-3: R-3 environment workaround is incomplete. The handoff for M100-M103 says 'unset MP_HOME' to run raul tests/CLI locally, but that is insufficient: ~/.agents/master-plan/bin is on PATH from the global install and predates M100, so raul's find_mp (crates/raul/src/mp_runner.rs:27) resolves the stale installed binary even with MP_HOME unset. Reproduced: 'env -u MP_HOME raul path --all' fails with 'unexpected argument --all' because the installed mp lacks the new flags. Verified workaround: 'PATH=$PWD/target/release:$PATH env -u MP_HOME raul path --all'. The honest guidance is either (a) document the PATH requirement in master-plan/AGENTS.md dev section, or (b) make raul's find_mp prefer a sibling target/release/mp when raul itself runs from target/, so dev mode Just Works. Option (b) is the structural fix; option (a) is a stopgap. Blocks confident end-user testing of the rc until make install refreshes the global binary.

items.description: F-6: lifecycle-aware gate reads are inconsistent (L24 pattern). validate/plan.rs reads legacy spec_status/execution_status directly in some gates (e.g. line 82 'm.milestone.spec_status == ready', line 106 '== verified', lines 130-132 draft/interview/review checks) and effective_lifecycle() in others (lines 78, 415, 437). Today this is consistent because the 102 dogfood milestones still carry populated legacy fields. But once the bulk lifecycle migration (migrate_plan_lifecycle, already shipped) runs and clears legacy fields, the direct-read gates become DEAD BRANCHES — they check fields that are now empty. Concretely: after migration, a milestone at lifecycle=approved would fail the 'spec_status == ready' check (empty != ready) and the gate would not recognize it as ready. This is a post-migration cliff: the migration utility is correct and tested in isolation, but its post-condition (gates still fire correctly after legacy fields are cleared) is NOT tested end-to-end. Fix: re-express G1-G14 to read effective_lifecycle() (or m.effective_lifecycle()) consistently, with a regression test that migrates a fixture and then runs validate to confirm gates still fire. MUST land before mp migrate lifecycle is callable in a release, otherwise running the migration silently disables gate conditions.
items.resolution: shipped: M104 commit c23880b (M105/M104 external review remediations)

items.description: B-58: Harden [block-cleared-on-complete: ...] annotation dedup in complete_milestone. The original M118 implementation dedup'd via substring match on the full annotation (which could falsely skip if the user-supplied prior_block_reason contained the literal '[block-cleared-on-complete:' substring). Worse, the original unconditionally overwrote verification.evidence with the new evidence_text, which silently DROPPED the annotation from the prior run on a re-completion. The dogfood-log-block-clear fix detects the annotation via a stable prefix '[block-cleared-on-complete:', carries any prior annotation forward across the evidence overwrite, and re-appends to the new evidence_text if missing. Pinned by complete_clears_block_on_success::block_annotation_dedup_on_repeated_complete + block_annotation_unique_even_when_reason_contains_marker_text. Status: shipped as M118.5 inline fix.
items.resolution: shipped: M118.5 inline fix tightens annotation dedup via prefix match + carries annotation forward across evidence overwrite; regression tests in crates/mp/tests/complete_clears_block_on_success.rs

items.description: Path review lane phase determination ignores execution_status (M101/M102/M103 show needs-self-check even though execution_status=blocked). In `crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs` the `review_lane` function matches on `lc.as_str() { \"done\" => Some(\"needs-self-check\"), ... }` — only the `lifecycle` field is consulted, not the `execution_status` overlay. So a done-lifecycle milestone that is also blocked (waiting for remediation) is mis-classified as self-check. Fix: 3-arm match on `(effective_lifecycle, effective_execution_status)` — e.g., `(done, blocked) => needs-remediation`; `(done, planned/in-progress) => needs-self-check`; `(done, in-progress+self-check) => awaiting-independent`. Pinned by a fixture test: a done-lifecycle + blocked-execution_status milestone shows `phase=needs-remediation` in the review lane. Workaround used in M125 release: nothing — the user has to read `mp status` blockers list to see the real phase. Filed during the M125 fold (commit `ab30f2e`) per the path review callout.
items.resolution: shipped:a618300 — fix(review-lane): classify (done, blocked) + sort by findings count (B-65, B-66)

items.description: Path review lane items tied at rank=1 (5 items in M100-chain review, no way to tell which to do first). In `crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs::review_lane` the `rank` field is the same for all `lifecycle=done` items (1u32). Visually the table shows M95/M100/M101/M102/M103 all at rank=1; reviewer cannot prioritize. Fix: sort by `(open_findings_count desc, milestone_id asc)` so the items with the most open findings come first; ties broken by milestone id (deterministic). 5-line change in the `sort_by` closure. Pinned by a fixture test: a review-lane fixture with 5 items having open-finding counts of 3, 0, 5, 1, 0 sorts to 5, 3, 1, 0, 0 in rank order. Filed during the M125 fold (commit `ab30f2e`) per the path review callout.

items.description: Parallel cargo test invocations race on workspace lock (~13/30 intermittent failures). When two `cargo test --test X` invocations run concurrently against the same workspace (e.g. suite_install + suite_milestone), ~13/30 runs produce intermittent spawn-failure or mp-command-failure panics at test setup. Layer 1 (recursive `cargo build --release` inside `mp install --dev` competing for `target/.cargo-lock`) was fixed in 2026-07-06 by removing `try_build_workspace` from `crates/mp/src/install.rs`. Layer 2 (parallel `target/debug/mp` spawn races between concurrent cargo test processes) is reduced but not eliminated by `pub fn run_with_retry` in `crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs`. Canonical CI pattern (`cargo test -p mp` with `--test-threads=1`) is fully green. Operational workaround: serialize cargo test invocations. Strategic fix options: (a) move all test binaries mp-spawn through a single binary launcher that serializes spawn; (b) build `target/debug/mp` once outside the test processes and have them all spawn that same artifact via a file-path dependency; (c) capture mp as a test fixture in a `tests/fixtures/bin/` directory checked in. Best filed as a follow-up — the canonical pattern is green.

items.description: External code review should be a mandatory gate before `lifecycle: complete` (or before close-out commits). Pattern observed across three post-close external reviews (M113, M114, M115, 2026-07-07): the close-out commits reliably fix evidence-uniqueness and verify-lint hygiene, but ship latent correctness bugs that only surface under a second-pass external review. Concrete cases: (1) M113 F-3 — `--dry-run` previews on approve/complete returned `{dry_run:true}` BEFORE running the gate checks the real commands enforce, so the preview reported success for inputs the real invocation would reject; (2) M114 F-1 — `mp edit strip-dropped-keys` / `migrate-lifecycle` rewrote milestone files WITHOUT the M113 advisory write lock (unlike `cmd_milestone`), reopening the exact concurrent-write race M113 AC-01 claimed closed; plus a misnamed `post_strip_validate_summary_stays_green` test that asserted only JSON validity, not the gate its name promised; (3) M115 F-1 — empty-visible layout returned `overflowed:false`, so `render_tab_bar` fell through to the wide branch and emitted all 7 lanes into a 1-col area (masked because ratatui clips the buffer). None were caught by the executor's self-review or the close-out evidence pass; all three were found by an external reviewer reading the same code. Proposal: add an AC to whichever milestone owns lifecycle/process (likely M100's lifecycle state machine, or a new process milestone) requiring a session-tagged external code review record (`mp reviews pass` from a session other than the executor's) as a gate on `complete`, mirroring the existing code-review gate on individual milestones (G15). Scope: the gate + a one-page reviewer checklist (correctness of new code paths, test-does-what-name-says, lock/gate coverage on every write path, magic-number provenance). Not a full audit pass — a focused second-pair-eyes check.

items.description:
[bug] review_state() unreachable "reviewed-clean" branch (reviews.rs:673).

The branch that returns "reviewed-clean" when findings exist AND at least one is neither open nor fixed is unreachable: the finding status model only has "open" and "fixed" (both literals). So the natural close-out path (remediate all findings -> mp reviews pass) lands on "remediated", never "reviewed-clean".
